newsitem.title: USA: US exchanges may not meet audit trail targets -GAO.
newsitem.headline: US exchanges may not meet audit trail targets -GAO.

text.p: The U.S. General Accounting Office (GAO) is concerned that U.S. futures exchanges may not meet federal regulatory standards established last year for tracking trades.
In a report to Congress released today, the GAO reviewed actions taken by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to improve audit trail systems at futures exchanges.
"We are concerned that the momentum toward achieving compliance could be lost," the report stated.

In August, the CFTC said two of the world's largest futures exchanges -- the Chicago Board of Trade and the Chicago Mercantile Exchange -- had audit trail systems that failed to meet standards originally set in the Futures Trading Practices Act of 1992.
Those standards demand 90 percent accuracy in monitoring trades. The exchanges have a deadline of January 1, 1997, to meet the standards.
The GAO said Wednesday the CBOT and CME "do not yet meet the heightened standards," and the implementation of electronic trading terminals to help do so is uncertain."

A bill to reform the Commodity Exchange Act introduced this month by Senators Richard Lugar, an Indiana Republican, and Patrick Leahy, a Vermont Democrat, would clarify audit trail requirements imposed by earlier legislation.

The bill would clarify the intent of Congress that the audit trail statute requires a minimum performance standard but does not mandate the use of any particular technology. The Lugar-Leahy bill is considered unlikely to pass this year but is expected to be revived next year.

The GAO report recommended that Congress be kept up to date on progress by the exchanges towards audit trail targets as well as other requirements in the act, and on any steps taken by the CFTC to ensure this is done. Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuter.com
